chunks: A man is afflicted by janabah while he has sores or wounds, or he fears the cold for himself. He said: “He does not perform ghusl; he performs tayammum.”
As for the report that he narrated:
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He said: I asked him about a man who is affected by janabah on a cold night and fears destruction for himself if he performs ghusl. He said: “He performs tayammum, and when he is safe from the cold, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat.”

key_terms.اَلتَّلَفَ: destruction or serious harm feared from bathing
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer to be repeated according to the report
key_terms.اَلْبَرْدَ: cold that poses a risk of harm
key_terms.اَلْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.جُرُوحٌ: wounds that may be harmed by water
key_terms.قُرُوحٌ: sores or ulcer-like injuries on the body
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone in janabah who fears harm from using water in severe cold or because of wounds?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a person in janabah who cannot safely perform ghusl because of wounds or severe cold. It permits tayammum in place of ghusl under fear of harm, and the second report states that once the danger passes, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat.
